```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Two rxode2 warnings are expected here and carry no information: the
# indicator-multiplexed IOV etas are not mu-referenced, and the solves pass
# their random effects as event-table columns with `omega = NA`.
quietly <- function(expr) {
  withCallingHandlers(expr, warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("non-mu referenced|multi-subject simulation without", conditionMessage(w))) {
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  })
}
```

# Model and source

Goeyvaerts et al. (2026) combined a population pharmacokinetic (PopPK) model
of the dengue antiviral mosnodenvir (JNJ-64281802) with a within-host viral
dynamic model (VDM) of serum DENV-3 RNA in a controlled human infection model
(CHIM), in which healthy volunteers took mosnodenvir as pre-exposure
prophylaxis and were then inoculated with the DENV-3 strain rDEN3delta30. The
two layers are linked sequentially: the PopPK model supplies each
participant's average steady-state concentration (Cavg,SS), and a sigmoid
Imax function of Cavg,SS inhibits virion production in the VDM.

The paper contributes three models:

| Model | Content |
|---|---|
| `Goeyvaerts_2026_mosnodenvir` | PopPK model (Supplement Table S2) |
| `Goeyvaerts_2026_mosnodenvir_vdm_c1` | Interim VDM fitted to Cohort 1, used to choose the Cohort 2 regimens (Table 2, C1 column) |
| `Goeyvaerts_2026_mosnodenvir_vdm` | Final VDM refitted to Cohorts 1 and 2 (Table 2, C1 and C2 column) |

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Goeyvaerts_2026_mosnodenvir"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.70439>

```{r descriptions, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
for (nm in c("Goeyvaerts_2026_mosnodenvir", "Goeyvaerts_2026_mosnodenvir_vdm_c1", "Goeyvaerts_2026_mosnodenvir_vdm")) {
  cat("* **", nm, "**: ", quietly(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(nm)))$description, "\n", sep = "")
}
```

# Population

**PopPK.** 8,352 plasma samples from 246 healthy adults in three Phase 1
studies (64281802DNG1001, DNG1006, DNG1008) and Cohort 1 of the Phase 2a CHIM
(64281802DNG2002), covering single doses of 50-1200 mg as oral solution,
tablet (fasted and fed) and capsule, daily dosing of the solution, once- or
twice-weekly dosing of the fed tablet after a BID loading phase, and the
Cohort 1 capsule regimens (Supplement Table S1). Cohort 2 data were not used
for estimation; individual Cohort 2 parameters were obtained by MAP Bayesian
estimation with the PopPK model as prior.

**VDM.** 54 participants of the Phase 2a CHIM (Table 1): Cohort 1 (n = 29;
placebo 7, high 600/200 mg, medium 200/50 mg and low 40/10 mg QD
loading/maintenance as fasted capsules) and Cohort 2 (n = 25; placebo 6,
daily 800 mg BID loading then 250 mg QD, weekly high 450 mg BID loading then
1200 mg weekly, weekly low 250 mg BID loading then 500 mg weekly, as fed
tablets). Median age 32 (Cohort 1) and 29 (Cohort 2) years; 65.5% and 52.0%
female; median BMI 27.1 and 24.4 kg/m^2. 1,047 serum samples, of which 86.6%
had undetectable DENV-3 RNA (below the 36 copies/mL limit of detection).

The same information is available programmatically via each model's
`population` metadata, e.g.
`readModelDb("Goeyvaerts_2026_mosnodenvir_vdm")()$population`.

# PopPK: virtual cohorts

Six regimens with 200 virtual participants each: the three Cohort 1 regimens
(fasted capsule; QD loading on Days -5 to -1, QD maintenance on Days 1-21) and
the three Cohort 2 regimens (fed tablet; BID loading on Days -2 and -1, then QD
maintenance on Days 1-21 or weekly maintenance on Days 1, 8 and 15). Time zero
is the first loading dose, so Day 1 (inoculation) starts at 120 h for Cohort 1
and 48 h for Cohort 2.

The paper sampled BMI from the pooled PopPK dataset, which is not published.
BMI is drawn here from a normal distribution with mean 25.5 and SD 4 kg/m^2,
truncated to 18-35 kg/m^2, which spans the Phase 2a range (18.2-34.7 kg/m^2,
Table 1) around the PopPK median of 24.7 kg/m^2.

Random effects are drawn in R and passed as columns of the event table, with
`omega = NA`, so the cohort is identical on every machine. As in the paper's
simulations, inter-occasion variability is left out (`OCC = 0`).

```{r pk-cohort}
set.seed(20260809)
n_per_arm <- 200

regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~cohort, ~ld, ~ld_ii, ~ld_n, ~md, ~md_ii, ~md_n, ~FED, ~FORM_CAPSULE,
  "C1 low dose", "Cohort 1", 40, 24, 5, 10, 24, 21, 0, 1,
  "C1 medium dose", "Cohort 1", 200, 24, 5, 50, 24, 21, 0, 1,
  "C1 high dose", "Cohort 1", 600, 24, 5, 200, 24, 21, 0, 1,
  "C2 daily dose", "Cohort 2", 800, 12, 4, 250, 24, 21, 1, 0,
  "C2 weekly high dose", "Cohort 2", 450, 12, 4, 1200, 168, 3, 1, 0,
  "C2 weekly low dose", "Cohort 2", 250, 12, 4, 500, 168, 3, 1, 0
)

pk_omega <- c(
  etalcl = 0.083445, etalvc = 0.23119, etalfdepot = 0.10516,
  etalka = 0.12701, etalktr = 0.19499
)

make_pk_arm <- function(i, n, id_offset) {
  r <- regimens[i, ]
  day1 <- r$ld_n * r$ld_ii # time of the first maintenance dose (Day 1)
  dose_times <- c((seq_len(r$ld_n) - 1) * r$ld_ii, day1 + (seq_len(r$md_n) - 1) * r$md_ii)
  dose_amts <- c(rep(r$ld, r$ld_n), rep(r$md, r$md_n))
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  subj <- tibble(id = ids, BMI = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, 25.5, 4), 18), 35))
  for (e in names(pk_omega)) subj[[e]] <- rnorm(n, 0, sqrt(pk_omega[[e]]))
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, tibble(time = dose_times, amt = dose_amts)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = seq(0, day1 + 28 * 24, by = 1)) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    group_by(id) |>
    # DOSE_MOSNODENVIR_MG carries the amount of the most recent dose record.
    mutate(DOSE_MOSNODENVIR_MG = ifelse(evid == 1L, amt, NA_real_)) |>
    tidyr::fill(DOSE_MOSNODENVIR_MG, .direction = "downup") |>
    ungroup() |>
    left_join(subj, by = "id") |>
    mutate(
      regimen = r$regimen, cohort = r$cohort, day1 = day1,
      md = r$md, md_ii = r$md_ii,
      FED = r$FED, FORM_CAPSULE = r$FORM_CAPSULE, FORM_SOLUTION = 0, OCC = 0L
    )
}

pk_events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  make_pk_arm(i, n_per_arm, id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per_arm)
})) |>
  mutate(amt = ifelse(is.na(amt), 0, amt)) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, cmt, everything())
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(pk_events[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))
```

```{r pk-simulate}
mod_pk <- quietly(readModelDb("Goeyvaerts_2026_mosnodenvir"))
sim_pk <- quietly(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_pk, pk_events,
  omega = NA, returnType = "data.frame",
  keep = c("regimen", "cohort", "day1", "md", "md_ii")
))
sim_pk$day <- (sim_pk$time - sim_pk$day1) / 24
```

## Figure 4: concentration-time profiles

```{r figure-4}
sim_pk |>
  group_by(cohort, regimen, day) |>
  summarise(mean_cc = mean(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(day, mean_cc, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(11800, 2180), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(~cohort) +
  labs(
    x = "Time relative to Day 1 (inoculation) (days)",
    y = "Mean mosnodenvir concentration (ng/mL)",
    colour = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 4 of Goeyvaerts 2026 (mean profiles; the paper also",
      "shows 95% intervals\nacross study replicates). Dashed lines: NOAEL mean",
      "Cmax 11,800 ng/mL and interim typical RMIC 2,180 ng/mL."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

As in the paper, the C2 daily-dose maintenance concentrations sit above the
C1 high dose, the C2 weekly high dose fluctuates around the C1 high dose with
higher peaks, and the C2 weekly low dose lies between the C1 medium and high
doses.

## PKNCA: Table S4 exposure metrics

Table S4 reports the mean (SD) Cmax and AUC24h of the Cohort 2 regimens on the
day of highest exposure: Day -1 (the second loading day) for the daily
regimen and Day 1 (the first 1200 or 500 mg weekly dose) for the weekly
regimens.

```{r pknca}
c2 <- sim_pk |>
  filter(cohort == "Cohort 2", !is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, regimen)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(c2, Cc ~ time | regimen + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  pk_events |>
    filter(evid == 1L, cohort == "Cohort 2") |>
    select(id, time, amt, regimen),
  amt ~ time | regimen + id
)
intervals <- data.frame(
  regimen = c("C2 daily dose", "C2 weekly high dose", "C2 weekly low dose"),
  start = c(24, 48, 48),
  end = c(48, 72, 72),
  cmax = TRUE,
  auclast = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

# Table S4 reports means, so the simulated results are averaged the same way
# before comparison.
sim_means <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast")) |>
  group_by(regimen, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(value = mean(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = value)

published_s4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~cmax, ~auclast,
  "C2 daily dose", 8580, 171000,
  "C2 weekly high dose", 8460, 166000,
  "C2 weekly low dose", 4050, 81100
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_means,
  reference = published_s4,
  by = "regimen",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", auclast = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs. published (Table S4) mean exposure; AUC is over the 24-h day. * differs by >20%.")

chk <- dplyr::inner_join(sim_means, published_s4, by = "regimen", suffix = c("_sim", "_pub"))
stopifnot(
  # A transcription error in CL/F, F or a volume moves these by tens of percent.
  all(abs(chk$cmax_sim / chk$cmax_pub - 1) < 0.15),
  all(abs(chk$auclast_sim / chk$auclast_pub - 1) < 0.15)
)
```

All three regimens agree with Table S4 to within a few percent.

# From PK to Cavg,SS

The VDM is driven by each participant's average concentration over the
maintenance dosing interval at steady state,
Cavg,SS = 1000 F D / (CL/F tau) ng/mL, with F and CL/F the individual values of
the PopPK model (the model returns them as `fdepot` and `cl`).

```{r cavg}
cavg <- sim_pk |>
  group_by(regimen, id) |>
  summarise(CAV = 1000 * first(fdepot) * first(md) / (first(cl) * first(md_ii)), .groups = "drop")

cavg |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(
    `Median Cavg,SS (ng/mL)` = median(CAV),
    `5th percentile` = quantile(CAV, 0.05),
    `95th percentile` = quantile(CAV, 0.95)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "Individual Cavg,SS by regimen.")
```

# Interim VDM (Cohort 1): Table 3

The paper chose the Cohort 2 regimens with the PopPK model and the interim
VDM, simulating 500 replicates of 6 participants per regimen, with IIV on
log10 phi and log10 IC50 but not on log10 V0, and without residual error. Here
200 participants per regimen (plus 200 on placebo) are simulated once; the
paper's "median number of participants with undetectable DENV-3 RNA" is
compared with 6 times the simulated proportion, and the medians of the AUC and
onset metrics with the population medians.

```{r vdm-c1-simulate}
mod_c1 <- readModelDb("Goeyvaerts_2026_mosnodenvir_vdm_c1")

set.seed(20260810)
vdm_subj <- bind_rows(
  cavg,
  tibble(regimen = "Placebo", id = 10000L + seq_len(n_per_arm), CAV = 0)
) |>
  mutate(
    etalic50 = rnorm(n(), 0, sqrt(1.1927746)),
    etalphi_immune = rnorm(n(), 0, sqrt(0.4100762)),
    etalrbase_virus = 0
  )

vdm_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 28, by = 0.25), 0:84)))
vdm_events <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = vdm_subj$id, time = vdm_grid) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "virus") |>
  left_join(vdm_subj, by = "id") |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, cmt, everything())

sim_c1 <- quietly(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_c1, vdm_events,
  omega = NA, returnType = "data.frame", keep = "regimen"
))
```

```{r table-3}
lod <- 36 # copies/mL

vdm_metrics <- function(sim) {
  sim |>
    group_by(regimen, id) |>
    summarise(
      undetectable_d29 = all(viral_load[time <= 28] < lod),
      auc_vl = {
        k <- time <= 28
        log10(sum(diff(time[k]) * (head(viral_load[k], -1) + tail(viral_load[k], -1)) / 2))
      },
      # Study day of the first daily sample with detectable RNA (Day 1 =
      # inoculation); Inf when RNA stays undetectable through Day 85.
      onset_day = {
        d <- time[time %in% 0:84 & viral_load >= lod]
        if (length(d)) min(d) + 1 else Inf
      },
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

summ_c1 <- vdm_metrics(sim_c1) |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(
    n_undetectable_of_6 = 6 * mean(undetectable_d29),
    auc_median = median(auc_vl),
    onset_median = median(onset_day),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

published_t3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~n_undetectable_pub, ~auc_pub, ~onset_pub,
  "Placebo", 0, 5.02, "3.0",
  "C1 low dose", 0, 4.80, "3.0",
  "C1 medium dose", 2, 4.03, "9.0",
  "C1 high dose", 4, 1.50, "NA",
  "C2 daily dose", 5, 1.20, "NA",
  "C2 weekly high dose", 5, 1.34, "NA",
  "C2 weekly low dose", 3, 2.66, "46"
)

t3 <- inner_join(published_t3, summ_c1, by = "regimen")
t3 |>
  mutate(onset_median = ifelse(is.finite(onset_median), format(onset_median), "not reached")) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Regimen = regimen,
    "Undetectable to Day 29, paper (of 6)" = n_undetectable_pub,
    "Undetectable to Day 29, simulated (of 6)" = n_undetectable_of_6,
    "AUC D1-D29 (VL), paper (log10 copies*day/mL)" = auc_pub,
    "AUC D1-D29 (VL), simulated" = auc_median,
    "Days to onset, paper (NA = median not reached)" = onset_pub,
    "Days to onset, simulated" = onset_median
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Replicates Table 3 of Goeyvaerts 2026 (interim Cohort 1 VDM).")

stopifnot(
  # Counts: the paper reports medians of 6-participant replicates (integers).
  all(abs(t3$n_undetectable_of_6 - t3$n_undetectable_pub) <= 1),
  # AUC: a wrong IC50, Hill coefficient or viral kinetic constant shifts the
  # placebo and low-dose AUC by far more than this.
  all(abs(t3$auc_median - t3$auc_pub) < 0.5),
  # Untreated infection becomes detectable on study Day 3.
  t3$onset_median[t3$regimen == "Placebo"] == 3
)
```

The simulated counts, AUCs and onset days follow Table 3: no protection on
placebo or the low dose, partial protection on the medium dose and the C2
weekly low dose, and the median participant staying undetectable through Day
85 on the C1 high, C2 daily and C2 weekly high doses. The simulated
undetectable counts are proportions times 6 rather than the median of
6-participant replicates, so they are not integers.

# Reproductive numbers and RMIC: Figure 2

The basic reproductive number R0 = pI beta T0 / (kV (kI + alpha A0)) does not
involve the drug, the effective reproductive number is
Re = (1 - eps_p) R0, and the reproduction minimum inhibitory concentration
RMIC = (R0 - 1)^(1/h) IC50 is the Cavg,SS at which Re = 1. The models return
all three as outputs.

```{r figure-2}
mod_final <- readModelDb("Goeyvaerts_2026_mosnodenvir_vdm")
cav_grid <- c(0, 10^seq(0, 4.5, length.out = 120))
typ_events <- tibble(id = seq_along(cav_grid), time = 0, evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "virus", CAV = cav_grid)

re_curve <- bind_rows(
  quietly(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_c1), typ_events, returnType = "data.frame")) |>
    mutate(model = "(a) Cohort 1 (interim)", CAV = cav_grid),
  quietly(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_final), typ_events, returnType = "data.frame")) |>
    mutate(model = "(b) Cohorts 1 and 2 (final)", CAV = cav_grid)
)

derived <- re_curve |>
  group_by(model) |>
  summarise(R0 = first(R0), RMIC = first(rmic), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(derived, digits = c(0, 1, 0), caption = "Typical R0 and RMIC (paper: 28.7 and 2,180 ng/mL interim; 21.7 and 1,410 ng/mL final).")

stopifnot(
  abs(derived$R0 - c(28.7, 21.7)) < 0.1,
  abs(derived$RMIC / c(2180, 1410) - 1) < 0.01
)

ggplot(filter(re_curve, CAV > 0), aes(CAV, Re)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_vline(data = derived, aes(xintercept = RMIC), colour = "steelblue") +
  facet_wrap(~model) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Mosnodenvir Cavg,SS (ng/mL)", y = "Effective reproductive number Re",
    caption = "Replicates the population curves of Figure 2 of Goeyvaerts 2026."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Final VDM (Cohorts 1 and 2)

The final model, refitted to both cohorts, has a lower R0 (21.7) and IC50
(200 ng/mL) but larger IIV on IC50. The paper reports the observed Cohort 2
outcome rather than new simulations: participants with undetectable DENV-3 RNA
through Day 29 were 4/6 (daily), 5/6 (weekly high), 5/6 (weekly low) and 0/6
(placebo) (Discussion). The final model's predictions for the same virtual
participants are shown for orientation; they are not a fitted quantity and
are not gated.

```{r vdm-final}
set.seed(20260811)
vdm_subj_final <- vdm_subj |>
  mutate(
    etalic50 = rnorm(n(), 0, sqrt(2.3446155)),
    etalphi_immune = rnorm(n(), 0, sqrt(0.3715956))
  )
vdm_events_final <- vdm_events |>
  select(-etalic50, -etalphi_immune) |>
  left_join(vdm_subj_final |> select(id, etalic50, etalphi_immune), by = "id")

sim_final <- quietly(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_final, vdm_events_final,
  omega = NA, returnType = "data.frame", keep = "regimen"
))

vdm_metrics(sim_final) |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(
    "Undetectable to Day 29 (of 6)" = 6 * mean(undetectable_d29),
    "Median AUC D1-D29 (VL)" = median(auc_vl),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(Regimen = regimen) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Final VDM predictions for the same virtual participants.")

sim_final |>
  filter(time <= 42) |>
  # Fully suppressed virus decays towards zero and the integrator can return
  # tiny negative values; floor at 0.1 copies/mL for the log axis.
  mutate(viral_load = pmax(viral_load, 0.1)) |>
  group_by(regimen, time) |>
  summarise(
    med = median(viral_load), lo = quantile(viral_load, 0.1),
    hi = quantile(viral_load, 0.9), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(36, 1000), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time since inoculation (days)", y = "DENV-3 RNA (copies/mL)",
    caption = paste(
      "Final VDM: median and 10th-90th percentiles; dashed lines LOD (36) and",
      "LLOQ (1,000 copies/mL).\nValues below 0.1 copies/mL are drawn at 0.1."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Two VDMs.** Table 2 reports the interim model (Cohort 1) and the final
  model (Cohorts 1 and 2) side by side. Both are packaged: the interim model is
  what the paper's dose-selection simulations (Figure 4 RMIC line, Table 3)
  used, and the final model is the paper's headline result (R0 = 21.7,
  RMIC = 1,410 ng/mL).
- **Sequential linkage through Cavg,SS.** The VDM takes Cavg,SS as the `CAV`
  covariate, constant over the infection course, exactly as the paper's model
  does (the Discussion explains why a time-varying concentration was not
  used). It is computed outside the models from the PopPK `fdepot` and `cl`.
- **Log10-scale parameters converted to natural log.** The VDM was estimated
  with V0, beta, phi, pI, alpha, T0 and IC50 on the log10 scale and additive
  IIV on log10 V0, log10 phi and log10 IC50. The package stores
  `log(10^x)` for each, and the IIV variance as
  (ln 10 x CV x |theta|)^2, using the Table 2 footnote definition
  CV% = sqrt(omega^2)/|theta| x 100 with theta on the log10 scale. The log10
  IC50 is taken as log10 of the reported IC50 (200 or 263 ng/mL).
- **Target-cell production.** The paper names a zero-order production rate bT
  but reports no value. bT = kT T0 is used, which keeps target cells at T0
  before infection and is the disease-free equilibrium that the
  Supplement's R0 expression assumes.
- **Initial conditions.** At inoculation (time 0) T = T0, I = 0, V = V0 and
  A = A0, following the paper's definitions of V0 (baseline viral load), T0
  and A0.
- **Residual errors.** The VDM's additive error on natural-log RNA is encoded
  as `lnorm(expSd)` on `viral_load`. The PopPK "proportional" error is
  reported with CV% = sqrt(exp(sigma^2) - 1), i.e. a log-scale variance, and is
  encoded as `lnorm(expSd)` with expSd = sqrt(log(1 + 0.153^2)) = 0.1521.
  Censoring below the LOD (M3) and the LLOQ/2 imputation are estimation
  devices and are not part of the simulation model.
- **Formulation and food.** Only the tablet was given fed. The model maps
  FED = 1 to the fed-tablet F (reference, 1), Ka and KTR; the capsule and the
  solution were studied fasted only, and their F and Ka do not depend on FED.
  BMI multiplies every formulation's F, as the supplement states a single BMI
  effect on F.
- **Inter-occasion variability.** The IOV on F and KTR is encoded for two
  occasions (`OCC` = 1 or 2, a shared variance), matching the two-period
  crossover studies it was introduced for; `OCC = 0` turns it off. The number
  of occasions per participant in the pooled data is not reported.
- **Dose-selection simulations.** The paper ran 500 replicates of 6
  participants; this article runs one cohort of 200 per regimen and compares
  6 times the simulated proportion with the paper's median count. BMI was
  sampled from a truncated normal distribution, because the pooled PopPK
  dataset is not available. Table 3's AUC D1-D29 (VL) is taken as log10 of the
  trapezoidal AUC of linear-scale RNA from inoculation to Day 29, evaluated on
  a 6-hour grid; the paper's sampling grid for this metric is not stated.
- **Errata.** No correction notice for this article was found as of
  2026-11-16.
